questions.question: What are the primary colors in the traditional subtractive painting model?
What color results from mixing blue and yellow pigment?
What are complementary colors?
choices: Colors opposite each other on a color wheel

questions.question: What effect can complementary colors create when placed together?
What are analogous colors?
choices: Colors next to one another on the color wheel

questions.question: What is hue?
choices: How light or dark it is
A color's basic family or name
How muted or intense it is
The surface it is painted on

questions.question: What does value describe in color?
choices: Its place on the wheel only
The amount of pigment in a tube

questions.question: What does saturation describe?
choices: The intensity or purity of a color

questions.question: How can adding white to a hue affect it?
How can adding black to a hue affect it?
What are warm colors often associated with in a composition?
Why should artists consider color contrast for readable text?
choices: Text color determines the paper size
Low contrast makes all details clearer
Sufficient contrast helps viewers distinguish text from its background

questions.question: What is a neutral color?
choices: A color such as gray, black, white, or brown that is less strongly associated with a hue
Any color mixed from two primaries
A color that is always bright

questions.question: A painting feels overly intense. Which change may soften the palette?
choices: Use less saturated colors or add neutral mixtures
Use only complementary pairs at full intensity

questions.question: What is color temperature?
choices: The perceived warmth or coolness of a color
The amount of water in a brush

questions.question: Which pair is complementary in the traditional color wheel?
How can a limited palette help an artist?
choices: It can create harmony and focus choices
It removes the need for value

questions.question: Why can color meaning vary across contexts?
choices: Every color has one universal meaning
Culture, setting, and personal experience influence interpretation
Color meaning depends only on pigment brand
Context affects value but not meaning

questions.question: What is simultaneous contrast?
choices: A pair of colors mixed together
A color can appear different depending on the colors around it
An effect created only by black paint

questions.question: A designer wants an alert to stand out from a blue background. What is a reasonable strategy?
choices: Use nearly the same blue value
Put the alert in the smallest type
Choose a contrasting hue and check readability
